newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car imports seen growing 5 pct in '97--JAIA.
newsitem.headline: Japan car imports seen growing 5 pct in '97--JAIA.

text.p: Sales of foreign-made cars in Japan in 1997 are expected to be about five percent higher than in the current year, the Japan Automobile Importers' Association said on Thursday.

"We cannot expect as large increases as we enjoyed for the last few years but we expect further efforts in boosting car imports and forecast relatively firm growth for 1997," the association said in a statement.
It forecast sales of about 450,000 imported vehicles in 1997, up from an estimated 430,000 this year.
Of the expected 450,000 units, 415,000 will be passenger cars and 35,000 will be buses and other types of vehicles, JAIA said.
The 430,000 units expected to be sold in 1996 would be a 10.8 percent increase over last year, it said.

The association said it expected the smaller increase in 1997 because of a planned consumption tax rise in Japan next April and the yen's weaker trend. Japanese car makers are also expected to reduce exports to Japan from their overseas units, the association said.
Competition from domestically made cars will also be tougher as several new models will be introduced next year, the association said.
But it added that an increasing number of car dealers are expected to start selling imported cars.
The association said earlier this month that imported vehicle sales rose 4.1 percent in November from a year earlier to 35,933 units.
That brought sales of imported vehicles in the first 11 months to 389,466 vehicles, topping the 388,162 for all of 1995.
